description: Two additive oscillators of up to sixteen partials each, each able to modulate the other's frequency through zero

params.text: Sets how far the other oscillator modulates this one's frequency, 0 to 300 per cent
Sets how many partials its oscillator adds, 1 to 16
Sets how quickly the partials of its oscillator fall away towards the top, 0.1 to 3
Tilts its oscillator between odd and even partials, -1 to 1; at 0 both are heard, at -1 the odd ones alone and at 1 the even ones alone
Sets which partial its oscillator starts from, 0 to 24, so the fundamental and the partials below it are left out
Stretches the spacing of the partials of its oscillator, -1.25 to 1.25; away from 0 they stop being whole multiples and the sound turns metallic
Sets the ratio its oscillator runs at against the pitch, -32 to 32; below 1 the ratio is turned upside down, which gives the divisions
Adds a fraction to the ratio of its oscillator, -1 to 1
Attenuates the voltage at the FM CV jack before it is added to the FM knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Decay jack before it is added to the Decay knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Odd/Even jack before it is added to the Odd/Even knob, 0 to 100 per cent
Attenuates the voltage at the Stretch jack before it is added to the Stretch knob, 0 to 100 per cent

inputs.text: Modulates that amount, scaled by the FM CV knob
Modulates that fall-off, one per volt scaled by the Decay CV knob
Modulates that tilt, a tenth per volt scaled by the Odd/Even CV knob
Modulates that stretching, scaled by the Stretch CV knob
Sets the ratio of its oscillator by cable, 3.2 steps per volt, and moves the knob while it is patched
Sets that fraction by cable, a tenth per volt, and moves the knob while it is patched
Sets that number by cable, 1.6 partials per volt, and moves the knob while it is patched
Sets that first partial by cable, 1.6 partials per volt, and moves the knob while it is patched
Sets the pitch of both oscillators by cable, 1V per octave, one channel per voice

outputs.text: The wave of its oscillator, -5V to 5V

notes: the frequency modulation is always between the two oscillators: each one is modulated by the other's output at the amount set on its own side, so turning up both FM knobs gives cross modulation
the modulation is added to the frequency in hertz rather than to the pitch, so it passes through zero and stays in tune
the ratio, fine, partial count and first partial jacks move their knobs, and are read once every 32 samples
